skeleton:
Crispy Breakfast Potato Cubes

British · Easy · Serves 4

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The café's "home fries" — potato cut into small cubes, par-boiled, then fried in fat until every face is crisp and the insides stay fluffy. They are the hash brown's honest cousin: less engineered, more forgiving, and better at soaking up egg yolk, because the cube's corners catch crust while its faces hold the soft middle. One pan, twenty minutes, and the full English's potato slot is filled with something better than anything frozen. The method is the steam-fry: cubes par-boiled until just tender, then fried covered to finish cooking through, then uncovered to build crust on three or four faces. The two-stage cook is what lets a home pan do what a caff griddle does all morning.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The potatoes

- **Uniform 2 cm cubes** — the whole method depends on one cooking window. Lumps cook unevenly and the small bits burn before the big bits crisp. - **Par-boil to just-tender, not soft:** 6–7 minutes in boiling salted water, until a knife tip enters with slight resistance. Fully cooked cubes fall apart in the fry; barely-tender ones finish in the pan. - **Drain and steam-dry 3 minutes** in the colander — surface water is the crust's first enemy, as with every potato on this site.

Crispy Breakfast Potato Cubes

Prep: 10 minutes · Cook: 20 minutes · Total: 30 minutes · Serves 4

Ingredients

The potatoes

  • 700 g floury potatoes (Maris Piper), cut into 2 cm cubes
  • 30 ml / 28 g of bacon fat, goose fat, or a 50/50 butter-oil mix (15 g butter plus 15 ml oil)
  • 1 small onion (100 g), diced (optional but classic)
  • 3 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g smoked paprika (optional)
  • 1 g black pepper
  • 5 g fresh rosemary or thyme, chopped (optional)

Instructions

  1. **Par-boil and dry.** Boil the cubes in well-salted water 6–7 minutes, drain, and let them sit in the colander 3 minutes to steam themselves dry. Shake once to roughen the surfaces. Checkpoint — the cubes' edges look slightly fuzzy and matte — the roughened starch surface that catches crust — and no water drips when the colander is tilted.
  2. **Fry covered to finish through, 8 minutes.** Heat the fat in a wide heavy pan over medium heat until it shimmers. Add the cubes in one layer, toss to coat, then cover and cook 8 minutes, tossing once halfway. The lid steams them tender while the pan-fried base starts to colour. Checkpoint — a cube cut in half at the 8-minute mark is fluffy-tender all the way through, its faces just beginning to show pale gold. If the centres are still firm, 3 more minutes lidded.
  3. **Uncover and crisp, 6–8 minutes.** Add the onion (if using), the salt, pepper, paprika, and herbs. Raise the heat to medium-high and fry uncovered 6–8 minutes, turning only every 2 minutes with a firm spatula — each turn gives a new face its crust and lets the fond build in the pan. Checkpoint — at least three faces of most cubes are deep golden and crusty, the onion is browned at its edges and sweet, and the pan's fond is dark but not black. The cubes rattle when the pan is shaken — the sound of crust, not steam.
  4. **Serve hot, straight from the pan.** Season again lightly at the pan if needed, and land the cubes beside the eggs while they still rattle. Checkpoint — the eating test: crust crackles, interior fluffs, and the yolk that runs over them disappears into the crevices — the cube's whole purpose.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Cubes fell apartPar-boiled too long6–7 minutes to knife-resistance, not knife-soft
Pale and soft, no crustCrowded pan or no lid stageOne layer, the full steam-fry sequence
Burnt bits, raw centresHeat too high for the uncover stageMedium-high after the cubes are tender, not before
Greasy cubesToo much fat or no steam-dry30 ml for 700 g; the 3-minute colander rest

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Make-ahead:** par-boiled cubes hold 3 days refrigerated — the morning is then a 12-minute pan job. Cooked cubes re-crust in 5 minutes in a hot dry pan; they never microwave well. - **Variation — the bubble-adjacent version:** fry the cubes harder, to a deep all-over crust, and serve under a fried egg — halfway to the full-English hash. - **Variation — the Christmas version:** replace potato with par-boiled Brussels sprouts, halved, same method — the sprout fry-up's quiet revelation. - **On the plate:** these are the full English's standard potato, the hash's rougher sibling, and the rösti's easier cousin — one technique, three dishes, all better than frozen.
